types.oie_definition: A political entity representing a subdivision of a country with defined boundaries and governance.
types.embedding_query_text: State: A political entity representing a subdivision of a country with defined boundaries and governance. Also called Province, Region, Territory, Federal state.

chosen_type.label: State
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'Washington state' directly refers to a specific state in the US, aligning with the schema.org State definition.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement characterized by infrastructure, governance, and population density.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement characterized by infrastructure, governance, and population density. Also called Municipality, Urban area, Metropolis, Town.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'Spokane' is a well-known city, matching the schema.org City definition.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

types.oie_definition: An individual human being identified by a proper name or title.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being identified by a proper name or title. Also called Individual, Individual person, Named person, Public figure.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are proper names of individuals, fitting the schema.org Person definition.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.oie_definition: A quantitative measure of the number of people in a specified context.
types.embedding_query_text: Population: A quantitative measure of the number of people in a specified context. Also called Population count, Human count, People count, Resident count.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: The mention '60,000 people' represents a statistical group of people, aligning with schema.org StatisticalPopulation.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

types.oie_definition: A quantitative measure of the number of physical structures or buildings.
types.embedding_query_text: StructureCount: A quantitative measure of the number of physical structures or buildings. Also called Building count, Facility count, Property count, Infrastructure count.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: The mention '700 buildings' is a numerical count of structures, fitting schema.org QuantitativeValue.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: ApartmentComplex
candidates.comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.oie_definition: A structured group of individuals working toward a common purpose or goal.
types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of individuals working toward a common purpose or goal. Also called Agency, Institution, Corporation, Government body.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Both 'National Weather Service (NWS)' and 'Avista Utilities' are public-sector organizations, matching schema.org GovernmentOrganization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.oie_definition: A proper name assigned to a specific wildfire or group of wildfires for identification.
types.embedding_query_text: FireName: A proper name assigned to a specific wildfire or group of wildfires for identification. Also called Wildfire name, Incident name, Blaze identifier, Fire event name.

chosen_type.label: WildfireName
chosen_type.definition: A proper name assigned to a specific wildfire or group of wildfires for identification.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches wildfire naming conventions; 'WildfireName' is a new type under Event for structured identification.

candidates.label: FireStation
candidates.comment: A FireStation is a CivicStructure housing firemen and fire-fighting equipment. Also called fire department, firehouse. Examples: The local city fire station, a volunteer fire department, a regional fire and rescue service.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: RsvpResponseType
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type. Examples: RsvpResponseType.Yes, RsvpResponseType.No, RsvpResponseType.MayBe.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.

types.oie_definition: A specific point in time or time span denoted by calendar date components.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time or time span denoted by calendar date components. Also called Calendar date, Temporal marker, Time reference, Chronological point.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The mention '2026-08-04' is a specific calendar date, fitting schema.org Date. Other mentions are relative/recurring but 'Date' is the most precise match.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.oie_definition: A quantitative measure of the number of individuals or entities receiving a service or product.
types.embedding_query_text: CustomerCount: A quantitative measure of the number of individuals or entities receiving a service or product. Also called Service recipient count, User count, Client count, Subscriber count.

chosen_type.label: InteractionCounter
chosen_type.justification: The mention '10,000 electricity customers' is a quantitative metric of service users, aligning with schema.org InteractionCounter.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: DepositAccount
candidates.comment: A type of bank account primarily used for depositing funds, often to earn interest or other benefits. Also called Savings account, checking account, current account, money market account. Examples: A personal savings account, a business checking account, a certificate of deposit (CD). Distinct from LoanOrCredit, which represents borrowed funds.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: MemberProgram
candidates.comment: An intangible loyalty or membership program that offers specific benefits to its members. Also called loyalty program, membership scheme, rewards program. Examples: an airline frequent flyer program, a supermarket loyalty card, a gym membership.

types.oie_definition: A figurative or non-literal characterization used to convey a specific meaning.
types.embedding_query_text: MetaphoricalDescription: A figurative or non-literal characterization used to convey a specific meaning. Also called Figurative phrase, Symbolic expression, Idiomatic description, Analogical reference.

chosen_type.label: MetaphoricalDescription
chosen_type.definition: A figurative or non-literal characterization used to convey a specific meaning.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches metaphorical language; 'MetaphoricalDescription' is a new type under DefinedTerm to capture non-literal terms.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: Quotation
candidates.comment: A Quotation is a CreativeWork representing a passage or statement, often from a written work, attributable to an author. Also called quote, excerpt, citation. Examples: "To be or not to be, that is the question.", a famous saying, a line from a movie, a passage from a book.

types.oie_definition: A digital document accessible via the internet with a unique URL.
types.embedding_query_text: WebPage: A digital document accessible via the internet with a unique URL. Also called Online article, Digital page, Web resource, Internet document.

chosen_type.label: WebPage
chosen_type.justification: The URL 'https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3046g80yj7o' is a specific web page, matching schema.org WebPage.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: ContactPage
candidates.comment: A web page specifically designed to provide contact information for an entity. Also called contact us page, inquiry page, reach us page. Examples: A website's "Contact Us" page, a business's support page, a personal portfolio's contact section. Distinct from WebPage, which is a general web document.

candidates.label: ItemPage
candidates.comment: An ItemPage is a web page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel. Also called product page, detail page, single item view. Examples: an Amazon product page, a hotel booking page for a specific hotel, a blog post about one topic. Distinct from CollectionPage, which displays multiple items.

candidates.label: AboutPage
candidates.comment: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. Examples: The "About Us" section of a company website, a personal biography page, a project overview page.

candidates.label: MedicalWebPage
candidates.comment: A web page that specifically provides medical information. Also called health information page, clinical webpage, medical content page. Examples: a page describing a disease, a page explaining a medical procedure, a doctor's profile page. Distinct from WebPage, which is a broader category for any web document.
